statement: Extending a 'counted by its file name' rule to a new ecosystem asserts a negative for every idiom in that ecosystem the detector cannot read. A1 rates a name-shaped test file with no recognized assertion as hollow; adding *Tests.cs and *Spec.scala to that rule, as a card asked, would have called every FluentAssertions, Shouldly or specs2 test file hollow, a false assertion created by a recognition fix. Rule: when a name-based rule turns unrecognized content into a negative claim, extend it only to cases with affirmative evidence (here a documented suite-level skip), and pin a control file in an unread library that must stay out of the denominator.

An idiom matcher run over source text matches the import statements that name the idiom. 'import io.kotest.matchers.shouldBe' satisfied a shouldBe matcher with no matcher call in the file, and the existing raw 'should.' alternative credits every file importing ScalaTest's 'matchers.should.Matchers' (#486). Rule: search idioms with import lines blanked, and give every gated idiom a near-miss whose only occurrence of the idiom's name is its own import.

A test that reads a ratio metric must compute the ratio, not read the numerator. A1 non_hollow_test_share stores the non-hollow file count as value and the rated count as max; the earlier AVA tests read value alone, which agrees with the share only for 0-of-1 and 1-of-1 fixtures. Mixed fixtures (one live file, one skipped) read 1 where the share was 0.5. Rule: assert value/max, and include at least one fixture whose share is neither 0 nor 1.
